doc.title: Gene Bertoncini interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2001

title: Burt Bacharach dates
summary: He recalls how Bacharach appreciated his classical guitar fills.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: What were some of the pop acts that you might have played in the studio with?

Well I guess Burt Bachrach. I would consider him pop music. I mean it was good music in its own way. And he used to really get carried away with whatever little thing I did. “Oh man, you hear what he did there — bing!” Or something like that. And I loved it. And of course it was nice to be appreciated. And I loved a date where I could be creative a little bit and on Burt’s dates too, I used to do these classical guitar fills that he liked a lot. And I liked when I had a line to play though, mostly. If it was a film date or the guitar had a melodic line to play, instead of just a lead sheet of some kind.
